correctness.rationale: For arbitrary integral path lengths >=2, a connected initial set with neither terminal cannot enter two wholly empty paths; with one terminal it is equivalent to two or three nonempty path prefixes; with both terminals it is equivalent to an end-prefix union on every path, at least one full internal path, and at most one empty path. Degree-two internal forcing and the degree-three terminal obstruction prove necessity and sufficiency in all cases. The enumerators count (j+1) proper endpoint unions and one full union; no double counting across disjoint terminal cases. Exact standalone exhaustive bitmask simulation on 68 theta instances, 1,886,304 vertex subsets, confirms every coefficient and the six minima, as corroboration rather than infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026-11-07 tree polynomial paper proposes a general graph extension but gives no theta census; the exact theta formula involves a new two-terminal/three-arm structural decomposition. Exhaustive published-finding corpus searches with forcing/polynomial, theta/three paths, and connected variants identified theta findings on different parameters and forcing results on different graph families, not a statement implying the all-coefficient enumerator. The full motivating article was read and compared at the theorem and open-problem level. This is a best-knowledge originality judgment, not a proof that no unindexed work exists.

value.rationale: The 2026 tree connected-forcing polynomial opens a natural all-graph enumerative direction. Theta graphs are the basic nontrivial 2-connected, cyclomatic-number-two (series-parallel) class, and an unrestricted closed coefficient formula is a natural complete invariant and a reusable benchmark for propagation from two separated degree-three terminals. The invariant goes beyond the connected forcing number, and the universal six minimum sets across all arm lengths is a structural byproduct. It is neither an arbitrary finite restriction nor a previously tabulated scalar.
